evidence.note: Up-front architecture enumerates all subsystems (3 nodes, killable broadcaster, IRC, supervisor, shared SQLite, SPA) and designs start.sh/supervisor as a first-class component from the start rather than an afterthought.

Modular decomposition into db/util/store/bus/broadcaster/ws/irc/supervisor/ui, and early explicit recognition of the shared substrate: write_event() transactionally commits message+event and advances a dense per-channel seq — the highest-risk cross-cutting invariant identified as foundation.

Dependency-correct build order: db+store(seq)+bus/broadcaster foundations first, then auth/workspace/channel/message routes, then ws/irc, then supervisor last — dependents built on already-written foundations.
Mid-build revision: realized IRC bridging must survive killing node 0, so moved IRC out of node 0 into its own process — dependency-aware course correction.

Verification of each layer (health, cross-node seq density, WS fan-out, IRC seq, UI, resilience kill) came as one late batch rather than explicit per-milestone acceptance checks gating progression between milestones.

reasoning: The agent produced a sensible, dependency-correct ordered breakdown into major subsystems, recognized the critical shared substrate (dense per-channel seq, fan-out transport) early, and treated start.sh/supervision as a first-class concern — matching and partly exceeding the level-5 anchor. It even revised its design when a dependency (IRC surviving node death) surfaced. But it stops short of level 8: there is no explicit milestone hierarchy with per-milestone acceptance criteria; the build was one linear push with done-checks batched into a single late verification pass rather than milestone-gated. This places it between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 6.
